task.title: Customizable OpenRouter routing and model selection for recipe imports
task.description:
## Why
The recipe model provider work (branch `recipe-model-provider`) added OpenRouter as a provider, but only in its simplest form: one model slug in `RECIPE_AGENT_MODEL`, one key in `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, sent through the AI SDK's OpenAI-compatible provider. OpenRouter can do much more to control how a request is routed between models and upstream providers by price, performance and policy. None of that is exposed today. This story is deliberately unspecified; it records the idea and the questions to answer before speccing it.

## Current behaviour (starting point)
- `convex/lib/recipeModel.ts` resolves `{ provider, model, apiKey }` from deployment environment variables.
- `convex/recipeAgent.ts` builds the OpenRouter model with `createOpenAICompatible({ baseURL: "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", supportsStructuredOutputs: true })`.
- One model for every user and every import. No picker, no fallback, no routing preferences.
- The OpenRouter path is type-checked but has not been run against a live key.

## Ideas to evaluate (verify each against current OpenRouter docs first)
- Provider routing preferences per request: preferred provider order, allow or deny lists, whether fallbacks are allowed, sorting by price, throughput or latency, maximum price, and data-collection / privacy policy.
- Model fallbacks: an ordered list of models tried when the first is unavailable or errors.
- Routing shortcuts and auto-routing, if still offered (for example speed- or price-optimised variants of a model, or an automatic router).
- Restricting to models that support structured (JSON schema) output, since imports require it; ideally validated at configuration time rather than failing at import time.
- A model picker in the app: who may choose (deployment owner only, or each user from an owner-defined allow-list), and how to stop users spending the owner's credits on expensive models.
- Spend controls and visibility: per-key credit limits on the OpenRouter side, and recording per-import model, provider actually used, and cost if the API reports them.
- Whether to switch from the generic OpenAI-compatible provider to a dedicated OpenRouter AI SDK provider if that is what exposes these options cleanly.

## Open questions
- Is configuration deployment-level (environment variables or a settings table) or per-user?
- Which of these does the AI SDK path actually pass through, and which need raw request-body options?
- What should happen when no allowed provider supports structured output for the chosen model?
- Does any of this apply to the Anthropic and OpenAI providers, or is it OpenRouter-only?

## Acceptance (to be refined when specced)
- A written spec that picks a scope from the ideas above.
- The chosen routing controls are configurable without a code change and are covered by tests on the resolver.
- A live end-to-end import through OpenRouter has been run and recorded.

## Depends on
The `recipe-model-provider` branch being merged (upstream PR and/or the fork's `deploy` branch).
